Alembic Computer Services, Inc. is a small Arizona business software consultancy, not a data centre. The company sells custom programming, custom reporting and integration work built around QuickBooks and Acctivate inventory management software, together with point of sale connectors for retail systems including Blaze, Treez and Meadow. That is accounting and business systems consulting performed on other companies' software. It is not the business of leasing power, cooling and rack space, which is what a colocation or data centre facility does.

The stored coordinates resolve to 2125 South 48th Street in Tempe, Arizona, a mixed office and light industrial stretch near Phoenix Sky Harbor airport that holds a large number of small technology and services firms of exactly this kind. Nothing in the company's own published material describes server halls, uninterruptible power plant, standby generation or leased space for outside tenants, and this registry does not attribute any of those to it.

The map history shows how the classification arose and how little scrutiny it has had. The OpenStreetMap node was created on 28 May 2024 by a Maricopa County mapper working in iD over Bing aerial imagery, inside a 260 change edit whose comment reads road updates and building updates. The node has exactly two tags, the company name and telecom=data_center. It has no address tag, no operator, no website and no source note, it has never been edited since, and there is nothing in the object itself to check the classification against. The postal address in this record comes from reverse geocoding the coordinates, not from the map object.

The same mapper accounts for a recognisable pattern across the Phoenix area. A query over the metropolitan bounding box returns 54 objects tagged telecom=data_center, 19 of them last edited by this one contributor, and that set mixes genuine facilities such as Iron Mountain Data Centers AZS-1 and an EdgeCore building with software companies, a web development shop and a legal process serving business. A firm whose name contains the words Computer Services fits the pattern of a preset chosen on the strength of a name.

One further caution belongs on the record. The unrelated company at alembic.com, a causal analytics software vendor, is a different business with no connection to this listing, and the two should not be conflated.

reading.body:
This entry does not describe a data center. Alembic Computer Services is a software consulting firm providing accounting and business system integration services near Phoenix Sky Harbor Airport, not an operator of colocation infrastructure. The firm's own published materials describe custom programming, QuickBooks integration, and point of sale consulting work. No specifications for power capacity, cooling systems, or leased rack space are published.

The mapping of this address as a data center facility appears to be a classification error. The physical location sits in a mixed office and light industrial area of Tempe typical of small technology service firms, not in a zone or facility designed for server operations. Confirmatory research found no published evidence that this business owns or operates server halls, uninterruptible power systems, or colocation space for outside tenants.

This listing should be disregarded in any assessment of Arizona's data center capacity. Arizona has 56 mapped facilities in this database, but only four publish power figures totaling 512 MW. This entry contributes neither confirmed megawatts nor meaningful infrastructure to that total.
